clue.text: King tucked into fruit, very first from exotic tree

indicators.note: something tucked into another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
first from asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: R for Rex, Latin for king
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A king samples fruit from some rare foreign tree for the very first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic tree' reads as one phrase, but only 'tree' defines; 'exotic' just lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are tropical trees growing in coastal swamps, their roots arching above the salty water.

clue.text: Essential problem brought up with article about Bible

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards
about means surrounding, so the article wraps round the next piece

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A vital difficulty is raised about some piece of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A must-have is an indispensable item, the thing nobody can do without, exactly what essential describes as a noun.

clue.text: Travelling inspector taken into account under French name

indicators.note: one thing taken into another ends up inside it
in a down clue, under places this piece below the French word in the column

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A police inspector is booked under a French alias while on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places the inspector-in-account piece below the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples roam from place to place without a fixed home, so the adjective means wandering or itinerant.

clue.text: Tempo in class

blocks.note: second meaning: grade or quality, as in first-class

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests musical pace in a lesson; 'class' is really grade, as in first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means speed of progress and also a ranking or grade, as in a first-quality product.

clue.text: Vehicle on exercises, good at climbing, moving into position with clear view

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards
letters that are moving are shifted out of their order and rearranged

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A van labours uphill during training until it reaches a spot with a fine panorama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link to the definition, but it is anagram fodder along with the exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A vantage point is a spot giving a commanding outlook, such as a hilltop from which the surroundings are seen.

clue.text: Effect produced by demon with performance

blocks.note: an imp is a little demon

explanation.surface: A devil puts on a show and makes quite an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the influence or result something has, so it is a near synonym of effect as a noun.

clue.text: Old man, satisfied, raised beer in silence

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted to read upwards, so the word runs backwards
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: met as in a need met, satisfied

explanation.surface: A contented elderly gentleman lifts his pint without a word.
explanation.walkthrough: METHUSELAH is the Biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years; HUSH holds the upturned beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriarch of Genesis is the proverbial longest-lived person, so his name stands for any very aged fellow.

clue.text: Doubter ignoring pressure to support a hermit

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A sceptic who resists being pushed backs up a recluse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the shortened doubter goes under, so supports, the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic renounces comfort and worldly pleasure, often living in solitude like a religious recluse.

clue.text: Problematic god, name unknown

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A troublesome deity whose name nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny issue is full of difficulties, like a prickly bush that is hard to handle.

clue.text: Small issue with single interval

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A minor problem arises with one break in proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a noun, a problem, but it is the verb, to send out.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest musical step in Western music, the distance between adjacent piano keys.

clue.text: Snips round firm plaster

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Clippings are scattered around some solid plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal but here it turns the snips back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine render applied to walls and ceilings, a type of decorative plaster.

clue.text: Dim rebel went all over the place creating confusion

indicators.note: something all over the place is in disarray, so the letters are scattered and reordered

explanation.surface: A dim-witted rebel ran around wildly and sowed chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' belongs to the fodder, not the indicator: the signal is 'all over the place'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is a state of being puzzled and perplexed, a close synonym for mental confusion.

clue.text: Hard theory, endlessly obscure

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

blocks.note: H is hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A difficult theory that is endlessly unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective but is used as a verb, to conceal.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it from view, which is what hide means as a verb.

clue.text: Month consumed with detention of American novelist

indicators.note: detention means holding something in, so the next word is kept inside

explanation.surface: A month spent locked up, as reported by a writer from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen wrote Pride and Prejudice and Emma, making her one of the best-loved English authors of fiction.

clue.text: Primate holding very large cup almost showing sign of possession?

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so the primate surrounds the rest
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: OS is outsize, a clothing label for very large
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: An ape clutching a huge cup looks like it owns it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the punctuation mark in 's shows ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe followed by s marks the possessive in English, so it is literally a symbol indicating ownership.

clue.text: Unruly peers deny civic status of deputy leader

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters refuse to stay in order

explanation.surface: Rowdy members of the Lords refuse some honour to a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers are members of the House of Lords, the upper chamber of Britain's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-presidency is the office held by a second-in-command who stands in for a president.

clue.text: Harshness in treatment of irate spy

indicators.note: treatment means working on something, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry secret agent is roughly handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is roughness or severity of manner or tone, a formal synonym for sharpness and sternness.

clue.text: Game about to end in grief with prize going back in storage unit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the game wraps round everything that follows
end in asks for only the final letter of the next word
going back means travelling the wrong way, so that word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A game is about to finish in sorrow as the trophy is returned to the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' wraps and 'to' is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest of drawers is bedroom furniture with sliding compartments for keeping clothes, a classic piece of storage furniture.

clue.text: Popular measure without delay

blocks.note: a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A well-liked policy brought in at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To go hotfoot is to hurry somewhere in haste, so the adverb means immediately and speedily.

clue.text: Former partner writes invoice finally revealing cost

indicators.note: finally points to only the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex finally writes out the bill, showing how much was spent.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is money spent on something, so it is a synonym for the price or outlay involved.

clue.text: Movable icon in Java targeted

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A clickable symbol is aimed at in some Java code.
explanation.walkthrough: Java is a programming language, which keeps the computing surface consistent.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the figure representing a user on screen, a graphic that moves around in games or chat.

clue.text: Change round entire broadcast concerning treatment of animals

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the first word goes around the next
broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Change the whole programme about the care of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterinary means relating to the medical care of pets and livestock, as in a vet's surgery.

clue.text: Sword with items used regularly in set pieces

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A sword features among the props in staged fight scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: The epee is a fencing blade with a stiff triangular cross-section, one of three weapons in the sport.

clue.text: Centres of trade, bases doing deals for continent

indicators.note: centres asks for the middle letter of each following word

blocks.note: middle letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Trading hubs cutting deals across a whole continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's landmasses, stretching from Turkey to Japan.

clue.text: United in line after time in company

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
after places one piece behind another in order

blocks.note: U for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: United players queue up in time to join the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a touring group of performers, such as a theatre or dance company.

clue.text: Man, before large fall, foremost in investing capital

indicators.note: foremost means the very front, so only the opening letter is wanted
before places one piece ahead of the rest

explanation.surface: A man leads the way investing his money before a big market crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' sits in a money surface but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland, on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Artist at that point losing energy somewhat

indicators.note: losing a letter means dropping it from the word

blocks.note: there means at that place or point
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A painter at that stage is running a little low on energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather as an adverb means fairly or to some extent, the same moderating sense as somewhat.

clue.text: Approach filthy place inhabited by scoundrel, for example

indicators.note: a place inhabited by someone has them living inside it

explanation.surface: Coming near some squalid den where a villain lives, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' looks like a verb but is the noun, a plan of action.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a planned method for reaching a goal, a way of tackling a problem.
